claims.text: There is a significant positive statistical correlation between self-reported social media use and the spread of panic related to COVID-19 in Iraqi Kurdistan (R=.8701).
Facebook was the most widely used social media platform for obtaining COVID-19 information in Iraqi Kurdistan, used by 82.6% of respondents.
Fake news about COVID-19 was reported as the primary category of information creating panic on social media by 26.6% of participants.
Exposure to social media news during the COVID-19 outbreak psychologically affected 38.6% of survey participants.
Health news related to COVID-19 was the most followed news topic among social media users in Iraqi Kurdistan, read by 76.4% of respondents.

evidence.description: We found a significant positive statistical correlation between self-reported social media use and the spread of panic related to COVID-19 (R=.8701).
The majority of participants (426/516, 82.6%) used Facebook to acquire information about COVID-19.
Many participants (n=137, 26.6%) answered 'fake news about COVID-19' as having the most impact on creating panic on social media.
38.6% (n=199) of the participants were psychologically affected by the fear generated from social media posts.
The highest proportion of participants (n=394, 76.4%) had heard, seen, or read health news (COVID-19).

methodologies.name: Quantitative Online Survey and Content Analysis
methodologies.description: An online questionnaire administered in the Kurdish language to 516 social media users, analyzed using descriptive content analysis and statistical testing in SPSS.
datasets: Self-collected online survey data (N=516 social media users in Iraqi Kurdistan)
conditions: COVID-19 lockdown period in Iraqi Kurdistan

limitations.text: The study relies on self-reported data from self-selected participants.
The COVID-19 lockdown period constrained the ability to gather a more representative sample.
There was limited evidence prior to this study on the perception and impact of social media during a pandemic within non-Western communities.

future_work.text: Design courses and symposiums at universities to help students and faculty learn how to search for, evaluate, and discern health information during health crises.
Establish collaboration between media experts, health professionals, and governmental ministries to ensure only well-vetted information is disseminated during epidemics.
